questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

I have waiting / anxiously / for my / exam results.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **I have waiting**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original segment "**I have waiting**" lacks the auxiliary verb "**been**," which is necessary to form the present perfect continuous tense.
 
• In English, this tense is constructed with "**have been**" followed by the present participle (**waiting**).
 
• The** present perfect continuous** tense is used to describe actions or situations that started in the past, continue into the present, and may continue in future.
 
 
• **Structure**: Subject + has/have + been + present participle (verb + -ing)__
 
• **Example**: *They have been working hard.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, the **corrected sentence** is "*I have been waiting anxiously for my exam results.*"

Thus, **option 2** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

Rajiv __helps his friends of solve__ real-life problems with several methods and approaches.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**helps his friends to solve**" [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• The use of** ‘OF’ **in the underlined segment **“helps his friends of solve”** is **INCORRECT**.
 
• It should be **‘TO’ **in place of** ‘OF’**- **“helps his friends to solve”.**
 
• **‘TO’** is used here as an infinitive.
 
• The given sentence suggests that Rajiv assists his friends in the process of solving problems using various methods and approaches.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is “*Rajiv helps his friends to solve real-life problems with several methods and approaches*”.

Thus, **option 4** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__ **

 
• We can use **'solve' **without any preposition before it in this sentence.
 
• We use 'help' as a bare infinitive.
 
• "Rajiv helps his friends **solve **real-life problems with several methods and approaches."
 
• This sentence is also correct it conveys that Rajiv assists his friends in solving real-life problems, and these methods and approaches are part of the help he provides. It doesn't emphasize the act of solving as much as the given sentence(question).
 
• Both the forms are grammatically correct.
 
• We have to answer as per the options.

questions.question:

• The phrase "grease the palm" is an idiomatic expression used to mean giving someone a bribe. 
 
• This phrase alludes to the practice of applying grease to machinery to make it run smoothly. Similarly, when used metaphorically, it implies using bribe money to 'smooth' a transaction or deal.
 
• It implies illegal or unethical behavior, where money or other incentives are given to influence the behavior or decisions of another person.
 
• In the provided sentence, the businessman is said to agree to "grease the palm" of the bank manager. This clearly connotes that he is ready to bribe the manager to get his loan approved.

Hence, the correct answer is '**Option 4'**.
